title: American Needs More Urgency
summary_zh: 本期节目中，Brian Sumers 与 Brett Snyder 深度剖析了美国航空近期为追赶达美航空与美联航所采取的战略纠偏与高管洗牌。产品端，美航计划将窄体机高端座位占比从约25%提升至40%，并宣布全面恢复窄体机椅背娱乐屏幕及引入品牌零食。两人围绕美航枢纽网络能否消化 737 MAX 10 多达24个头等舱座位展开争论：Brett 担忧其缺乏北方核心商务市场支撑而陷入过度补偿，Brian 则认为高端休闲需求已普及至全美腹地。组织端，美航拆解了原先因人设岗的混乱高管职能，新任首席商务官 Nat Pieper 全面收拢客户体验与市场营销大权。两位主播一致认为，美航虽终于认错转向，但屏幕改装要到2028年才启动、人事调整仍缺乏问责魄力，整体转型严重缺乏紧迫感。
key_takeaways_zh: 美国航空计划将窄体机队的高端座位占比从25%大幅提升至40%，重点补齐加长腿部空间座位短板以撬动常旅客黏性与联名信用卡消费。
窄体机全面恢复椅背屏幕不仅能改善乘机体验并探索精准广告变现，更是向旅客直观传递高品质服务心智的关键视觉符号。
美航借高管离职理顺了此前混乱的汇报架构，首席商务官 Nat Pieper 整合客户服务与市场营销后权重大增，成为推动高端化转型的核心人物。
美航椅背屏幕安装需等到2028年才启动并延续至2030年代初，叠加上层沟通的保守官僚姿态，暴露出其在追赶竞争对手时严重缺乏紧迫感。

highlights.title_zh: 窄体机高端座位占比剑指40%
highlights.summary_zh: 美航计划在 A319、A320、A321neo 及未来的 737 MAX 10 上扩充头等舱与 Main Cabin Extra 座位，将窄体机高端座位占比从约25%提升至40%，直追美联航水平。Brian 指出，向精英会员免费提供加长腿部空间座位是激励常旅客保级和增加联名信用卡消费的核心手段。
highlights.quote_en: American said that its narrowbody fleet is going to go from about having a quarter of seats as premium all the way up to 40%.

highlights.title_zh: 激进扩充头等舱是否水土不服
highlights.summary_zh: Brett 质疑美航在北方大都市商务市场的网络规模不及达美与美联航，在 737 MAX 10 上配置24个头等舱座位恐属矫枉过正。Brian 则反驳称，如今高端休闲需求已席卷全美，连超低成本航司忠实航空都在增设头等舱，美航枢纽完全有能力售出这些座位。
highlights.quote_en: And when I look at American, I think 24 seats on a MAX 10 in first class, can it really sell all those?

highlights.title_zh: 窄体机全面恢复椅背娱乐屏幕
highlights.summary_zh: 美航彻底推翻了前美西航空管理层削减硬件成本的逻辑，宣布在窄体机队全面恢复椅背屏幕。Brian 与 Brett 认为，高清屏幕即使不被旅客打开使用，也能在登机瞬间营造高端客舱质感，未来更有望效仿美联航通过精准广告网络实现变现。
highlights.quote_en: So people get onto an airplane, they see the screens, particularly the newer screens with HD and the bright colors, and their brains register the cabin as having a better experience even if they never watch them.

highlights.title_zh: 硬件改装周期漫长缺乏紧迫感
highlights.summary_zh: 尽管美航终于掉头纠偏，但超过16万个窄体机座位的屏幕改装要到2028年才开始交付，并将一路拖延至2030年代初。Brett 指出，美航在战略摇摆中损失了宝贵时间，目前仅是在被动模仿竞争对手，而非做出引领行业的创新。
highlights.quote_en: But deliveries won't start until 2028, and it's going to take into the early part of the 2030s to get it done. That's a lifetime at this point.

highlights.title_zh: 高管洗牌与混乱组织架构拆解
highlights.summary_zh: 随着公关负责人 Ron DeFeo 与高管 Nate Gatten 离职，美航开始清理过去因人设岗遗留的奇葩架构，将美鹰航空划归运行部门，并将市场营销从公关部剥离。维修工程部虽引入前精神航空首席运营官执掌，但美航将人事变动包装为自愿离职的做法被批缺乏问责魄力。
highlights.quote_en: But there's a lot in American's org chart that's weird like this. I'm guessing it made sense to someone at some point just for this individual person

highlights.title_zh: 首席商务官集权与领导层焦虑
highlights.summary_zh: 首席商务官 Nat Pieper 将客户体验、呼叫中心、配餐及服务补救全部纳入麾下，终结了客户部门向商务与运行双线汇报的低效局面。尽管 Nat 深入一线的作风备受好评，但首席执行官 Robert Isom 在内部信中暗示后续仍有分批调整，反而加剧了组织内部的不确定性。
highlights.quote_en: I hate that they're talking about acting with greater urgency while simultaneously slow-rolling changes into multiple tranches with all this uncertainty.

highlights.title_zh: 引入品牌零食与重塑市场营销
highlights.summary_zh: 美航宣布在机上提供 Goldfish 品牌零食，并计划外聘首席营销官以重建品牌情感共鸣。Brian 肯定了品牌化细节与营销投入的价值，但 Brett 警告称，美航必须先修好运行基本盘并重振一线员工士气，否则过早宣传美好形象只会适得其反。
highlights.quote_en: Marketing isn't going to fix American Airlines. But if they do fix the airline, marketing is going to let people know that something has changed.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm Brian Sumers, and I write The Airline Observer.
transcript.zh: 我是 Brian Sumers，主理《The Airline Observer》。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And I'm Brett Snyder, author of Cranky Flier. You're listening to The Air Show, the podcast where we talk about what happens in the business of the sky. Thanks to this week's sponsor, Upgrade, Inc. Learn more at upgrade.com/flex-pay.
transcript.zh: 我是 Brett Snyder，《Cranky Flier》的创办人。欢迎收听 The Air Show，在这里我们畅聊航空商业界的风云变幻。感谢本周的赞助商 Upgrade, Inc.。了解更多请访问 upgrade.com/flex-pay。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Now Brian, you were on a long vacation on the other side of the world, and it, uh, did not go so well.
transcript.zh: Brian，你刚才在世界的另一头度了个长假，而且……看起来并不是很顺利啊。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, I do not know what you're talking about. How could any vacation that includes a ride on a Dash 8 and a Cessna Grand Caravan be so bad?
transcript.zh: Brett，我真不知道你在说什么。一段能坐上 Dash 8 和塞斯纳大篷车（Grand Caravan）的旅途，怎么可能会糟糕呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That is what I say every time I go to Molokai, but I'm pretty sure you had some, uh, non-aviation issues, shall we call it.
transcript.zh: 我每次去摩洛凯岛（Molokai）也是这么说的，但我敢肯定你遇到了一些……该怎么说呢，航空以外的麻烦。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Ah, yes, you mean that. Okay. Uh, I did learn something new on this trip, Brett. A cruise ship is not the only place where a mass of guests can get norovirus.
transcript.zh: 啊，对，你说那个啊。好吧，Brett，我这趟旅行确实涨了新姿势：游轮可不是唯一能让大批客人集体感染诺如病毒的地方。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It turns out that nearly every guest at a five-star hotel in the Serengeti can get norovirus at roughly the same time.
transcript.zh: 事实证明，塞伦盖蒂一家五星级酒店里几乎所有的住客，都能在差不多同一时间集体中招诺如病毒。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I did not get it nearly as bad as others who were with us, but let me tell you, uh, when your daughter is barfing in every corner of a hotel room, and I do mean every corner, at 2:00 a.m., the only people who can clean it up are mom and dad.
transcript.zh: 我的症状倒没有同行其他人那么严重，但听我说……凌晨两点，当你女儿在酒店房间的每一个角落吐得翻天覆地——我是说‘每一个’角落时，能收拾残局的就只有当爸妈的了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It was not great. There was one other indignity, as well. We missed a three-hour connection in Paris. Three hours, 180 minutes!
transcript.zh: 那场面别提多惨了。而且还不止这一件倒霉事。我们在巴黎还误了整整三小时的中转。三小时啊，180分钟！

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh, I'm sure you know the culprit: summer immigration lines, absolutely crazy, nuts. But life goes on, and honestly, I'm kind of glad that my kids got to see the other side of travel, the less glamorous one.
transcript.zh: 罪魁祸首你肯定猜得到：暑期入境海关排的长队，简直疯了，太离谱了。不过生活还得继续，而且说实话，我也挺高兴能让孩子们见识到旅行的另一面，不那么光鲜亮丽的一面。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That is rough. I do not deny that. But also funny as hell from my perspective. We've all been there, especially as parents.
transcript.zh: 那确实太惨了，我不否认。但站在我的角度看，简直好笑得不行。作为父母，我们都经历过那种时刻。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You do, however, seem to be alive now, so hopefully everyone is improving. Maybe that means we can do a show here, which is good, because I am glad you're back, even though Jon is not still back with us.
transcript.zh: 不过你现在看着还算健在，希望大家都慢慢好起来了。这也意味着我们可以正式录节目了，太好了。你回来了我很高兴，虽然 Jon 还没归队。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Jon won't be back until next month, and that's cuz we are taking our two-week end-of-summer break once this goes live.
transcript.zh: Jon 得下个月才回来，因为本期节目上线后，我们就要开启为期两周的夏末休假了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: We are indeed, but Brett, as you know, uh, this episode was very important to me. Some interesting stuff happened with one of my favorite airlines while I was on vacation, and I said we just had to do this this week.
transcript.zh: 确实如此。不过 Brett 你懂的，这期节目对我来说非常重要。我度假期间，我最喜欢的一家航司发生了一些很有意思的大动作，我当时就说这周非聊不可。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, this is true. Brian sent me a text from Africa, presumably while someone was throwing up in some corner, saying, quote, "Can I beg you to save the American episode for my return?" End quote.
transcript.zh: 确实是这样。Brian 从非洲给我发了条短信——估计当时正有人在某个角落吐呢——他说：“我能求求你把美航（American Airlines）那期留到我回来再录吗？”

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, I got a lot to say about this topic.
transcript.zh: 没错，关于这个话题我有太多话要说了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It's true, which means we should probably keep this thing moving because this is going to go long today, I think. But that is why we will be talking about American this week. I will say I would have loved to have talked about...
transcript.zh: 确实，这也意味着我们得抓紧时间了，因为我感觉今天肯定要超时。不过这也是我们本周要聚焦美航的原因。不过坦白说，我本来还挺想聊聊……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: at United flying to Okinawa and Ljubljana and all that. But that is going to have to wait because we're talking about what's been happening over the last month at American.
transcript.zh: 美联航新开飞往冲绳、卢布尔雅那等航线的事。但这些都得先放一放，因为我们今天要聊的是美航在过去这一个月里发生的大动作。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There's been organizational changes, in-seat videos coming back, adding premium seats. There is much to talk about here. So Brian, where should we start?
transcript.zh: 他们进行了组织架构调整、重新引入机上个人娱乐屏幕、增加高舱位座椅。这里面有太多看点。所以 Brian，我们先从哪儿聊起？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, a lot to discuss today, Brett. Let's start with the product, and then we'll move to the officer purge later in the show.
transcript.zh: 是的，Brett，今天确实有很多看点。我们先从客舱硬件产品开始，稍后在节目后半部分再聊高管层大清洗。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: First, Brett, we're finally getting more premium seats. And we've seen that a little bit on widebodies; now we're looking at narrowbody aircraft.
transcript.zh: 首先，Brett，美航终于要增加更多高舱位座椅了。我们在宽体机上已经看到了一些动作，现在轮到了窄体客机。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So here's what we think we know at this point. Details a little fuzzy. Looks like American is going to finish its plan to add an extra row in first class on the 319 and 320 fleets.
transcript.zh: 目前已知的大致情况是这样的，尽管细节还有点模糊。美航似乎打算落实计划，在 A319 和 A320 机队上增加一排头等舱。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: American is putting 24 first class seats on its MAX 10s when those get delivered. And then it looks like American is going to add first class seats to what is now a 20-seat premium cabin on the 321neo.
transcript.zh: 美航将在未来交付的 MAX 10 上配备 24 个头等舱座位。接着，美航似乎还打算在 A321neo 目前仅有 20 座的高端舱基础上增加更多头等舱座椅。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And then finally, we're going to get more extra legroom seats, Main Cabin Extra. So overall, American said that its narrowbody fleet is going to go from about having a quarter of seats as premium all the way up to 40%.
transcript.zh: 最后，他们还会增加更多额外腿部空间座椅，也就是 Main Cabin Extra。总体来看，美航表示其窄体机队的高舱位占比将从约四分之一一路提升至 40%。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And on that last stat, I am sure you are shocked that I went and pulled the numbers to see if they were...
transcript.zh: 关于最后这个数据，你肯定猜到了，我绝对忍不住去扒了一遍具体数字，想核实一下他们是不是……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Nerd.
transcript.zh: 真够书呆子的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, you know, we just got trust, but verify, right? So...
transcript.zh: 哎，你知道的，凡事都要“相信但要核实”，对吧？所以……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: If your mother says she loves you, check it out.
transcript.zh: 就算你妈说她爱你，也得去核实一下。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That's right. So I pulled just the narrowbody mainline fleet. I used fleet numbers from the end of 2025 in the 10-Ks.
transcript.zh: 没错！所以我单独拉出了美航干线窄体机队的数据。我依据的是其 10-K 年报中预测的 2025 年底机队规模。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I didn't include the 319 and 320 refits that they're doing. I assumed all the 321 work was done. I did exclude the two XLRs in the fleet at the time; that's a different product, that's a long-haul product.
transcript.zh: 我没有把正在进行的 A319 和 A320 改舱算进去；我假设 A321 的改装已全部完成；同时我剔除了届时机队中的两架 A321XLR，因为那是另一套客舱产品，属于远程机型。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So with that, plus all the 737s of course, I found that American had a total of 163,404 seats on its narrowbodies.
transcript.zh: 这样算下来，再加上所有的波音 737，我发现美航的窄体机共有 163,404 个座位。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And of those, 9.4% were in first, 16.3% in Main Cabin Extra, and 74.3% in regular coach. So yeah, that 25% current number rings true.
transcript.zh: 在这些座位中，9.4% 是头等舱，16.3% 是 Main Cabin Extra，普通经济舱占 74.3%。所以没错，他们说的目前约 25% 高端座位的说法确实符合实情。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: None of this, of course, exists in a vacuum. American says it's going to catch up to its competitors. How does this actually compare to United and Delta?
transcript.zh: 当然，这些举措脱离不了行业大背景。美航声称这是为了迎头赶上竞争对手。那么美航实际的情况跟美联航和达美相比究竟如何？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, see, I knew you were going to ask that, so of course I already had that pulled. Delta has about 10% in first and 20% in Delta Comfort+, so a total of only around 30% premium, which surprised me.
transcript.zh: 你看，我就知道你会问这个，所以我早就把数据拉出来了。达美的头等舱占比约为 10%，达美优悦经济舱（Delta Comfort+）占 20%，高端座位总计仅在 30% 左右，这还挺让我意外的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But United has the same first class percentage as Delta, but it has more than 28% of seats in Economy Plus. So it is closer to that American target of 40%.
transcript.zh: 而美联航的头等舱比例与达美相当，但其超值经济舱（Economy Plus）的座位比例超过了 28%。所以美联航更接近美航设定的 40% 目标。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's pretty interesting, Brett, that Delta is only at 30%. But I think that's probably going to change over time, especially as the 321neo...
transcript.zh: 达美居然只有 30%，确实挺耐人寻味的，Brett。不过我认为随着时间推移这很可能会发生变化，尤其是随着 A321neo……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Those come in, those are pretty premium heavy, then you have the older fleets like the A320, pretty premium light. So, I would imagine Delta's long-term target is probably closer to about 40%, right?
transcript.zh: 那些新飞机交付时，两舱及高端座位的配置比例相当高；但像A320这类较老的机队，高端座位占比又很低。所以我觉得，Delta的长期目标大概是接近40%左右，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Uh probably. I mean, I I haven't heard it said explicitly, I don't think. But...
transcript.zh: 呃，可能吧。我的意思是，我印象中他们好像还没明确这么表态过。不过……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Why would Delta tell us anything?
transcript.zh: Delta怎么可能会跟我们透露半点风声？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, that is a different issue, sir. But like, this this really, though, it it gets to the point that American is basically just trying to copy Delta and United's on-board experiences. And and I find that somewhat strange, considering they do run different networks, right?
transcript.zh: 好吧，那是另一码事了，先生。不过这确实触及了核心问题：American基本上就是在全盘抄袭Delta和United的机上客舱体验。我觉得这有点奇怪，毕竟两者的航线网络结构明明不一样，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: They do. United and Delta are larger in big business cities, especially in the northern half of the country, and I would imagine that historically speaking, American reasoned that it needed fewer premium seats because it had that different network and customer mix.
transcript.zh: 确实不同。United和Delta在大型商旅城市的体量更大，尤其是美国北部地区。而且我想，从历史上看，American当初的逻辑是，既然自身的航线网络和客群结构截然不同，自然不需要那么多高端舱位。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I still think, Brett, that was probably an old way of thinking. Premium seats, we have learned, do different things than they once did.
transcript.zh: 但我依然觉得，Brett，那恐怕是一种过时的思维方式了。我们现在明白，高端舱位发挥的作用已经今非昔比。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So, first, all over the country, paid load factors are up. And then, this is on all kinds of routes, it's not just on business routes. So, we hear so much now about premium leisure. First-class seats now profitable on their own, something that didn't quite exist 20 years ago.
transcript.zh: 首先，全美各地的付费客座率都在上升。而且这种情况出现在各类航线上，并不局限于商务航线。我们现在经常听到“高端休闲出行”这个词。头等舱座位如今单靠自身就能盈利，这在20年前简直不可想象。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And then second, we think about upgrades not in the way that we used to. So, 15 years ago or so, Delta started this new strategy that other airlines copied. Delta executives were adamant then that they could no longer give away their best product for free.
transcript.zh: 其次，我们现在看待升舱的角度也和以前大不相同。大约15年前，Delta开创了这项被其他航司纷纷效仿的新策略。当时Delta高管态度坚决地表示，绝不能再把自家最好的产品免费送人。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Uh, but over time, I I think Delta and United learned something else, that you can and probably should give away your second best product for free. That would be those extra legroom seats.
transcript.zh: 但随着时间推移，我认为Delta和United领悟到了另一层逻辑：你完全可以、甚至应该免费送出自己次好的产品。也就是那些拥有额外腿部空间的超级经济舱/舒适经济舱座位。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So, you give people a few extra inches of legroom, maybe a free snack or a drink depending on the airline, and they're going to stick around. And not only are they going to stick around, but they're going to do frankly irrational things to avoid paying the fee to actually sit there. They're going to spend more money on their credit card, they're going to try to climb that elite ladder.
transcript.zh: 你给乘客多让出几英寸的腿部空间，再根据航司政策送点免费零食或饮品，他们就会留下来。他们不仅会留下来，坦白说还会做出一些非理性的举动，只为了不花钱就能选坐那些位子。他们会更疯狂地刷联名信用卡消费，削尖脑袋往常旅客的高级别会员级别上爬。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: American's real problem up until maybe this announcement, in the domestic fleet, I don't think was necessarily the number of first-class seats. It's been this approach to Main Cabin Extra.
transcript.zh: 在这次官宣之前，American在国内航线机队上真正的硬伤，我认为倒未必是头等舱的数量，而是他们对待Main Cabin Extra（超享经济舱）的态度。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: We've seen a lot of airplanes that have like, what, three rows in the front, plus exit rows which are more narrow and not all that comfortable, just not enough extra legroom seats.
transcript.zh: 我们见过很多飞机，前排总共也就设了三排左右，再加上更窄且坐着并不怎么舒服的安全出口排，多余腿部空间的座位根本就不够。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, I do agree with you on Main Cabin Extra. There's no question that they needed more, and I don't think this was even a secret or required a great amount of thought, right? I think a lot of people were saying this for quite some time.
transcript.zh: 在Main Cabin Extra这一点上，我确实赞同你的看法。毫无疑问，他们需要增加更多此类舱位，而且我觉得这根本就不是什么秘密，也无需深思熟虑，对吧？其实很多人老早就一直在这么说了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Um, but American may be trying to overcompensate here is the way I look at this. It doesn't have a network like the others. I mean, of course it is a global premium carrier according to the CEO, but United and Delta are bigger...
transcript.zh: 但在我看来，American此举可能有点矫枉过正。它的航线网络跟那两家完全不同。我的意思是，虽然在CEO口中它是一家“全球高端航司”，但United和Delta的规模更大……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: ...in the bigger cities. And when I look at American, I think 24 seats on a MAX 10 in first class, can it really sell all those? And that's where I'm just not sure if this is just sort of a, we need to kind of overshoot.
transcript.zh: ……都在那些大城市。而当我审视American时，心想在MAX 10上放24个头等舱座位，他们真能卖得完吗？这就是我不确定的地方，不知道他们是不是有点矫枉过正、用力过猛了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, I think American can sell those seats. I get three types of complaints of my conduct here at The Air Show. The first is my voice, it's a little nasally. I can't do much about that, I'm sorry.
transcript.zh: Brett，我认为American能卖掉这些座位。听众对我在The Air Show上的表现主要有三类抱怨。第一类是我的声音，鼻音有点重。这我确实没办法，很抱歉。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The second is my politics. It seems like some of our listeners, probably airline pilots, don't like that. I'm not going to apologize for it.
transcript.zh: 第二类是我的政治立场。我们的一些听众，大概是航司飞行员吧，似乎不太喜欢这一点。对此我可不会道歉。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: This seems like a great time for us to give out your personal email address on air. Can we do that?
transcript.zh: 这听起来是个在节目里公布你私人邮箱的好时机啊。我们可以这么干吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, thank you. No, thank you.
transcript.zh: 别，谢谢你，千万别。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Okay, moving on.
transcript.zh: 好吧，继续往下说。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, the third complaint, I think is appropriate and I take it seriously. And that's that I'm a little bit too much of a coastal elitist who doesn't want to understand Middle America. And that's where I think American has a point here.
transcript.zh: 不，第三类抱怨我觉得很有道理，我也看得很重。那就是我有点太像沿海精英主义者了，不愿去理解美国中部地区。而这正是American有理的地方。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: There was this idea back in the day that the only people that bought first class were your lawyers, your consultants, and your bankers on the coasts. But things have changed a lot over the years.
transcript.zh: 过去人们总觉得，买头等舱的只有沿海地区的律师、顾问和银行家。但这些年来情况发生了很大变化。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: We now have Allegiant Air saying that premium is so hot that they are adding a first-class cabin called Allegiant First. It's going to be relatively small, not on every plane, but you can see that it's not just the coasts that want to fly in first class, it's everyone. I think American's hubs are fine for this new trend of who is buying first class.
transcript.zh: 如今连Allegiant Air都表示两舱需求极其火爆，他们正在增设名为“Allegiant First”的头等舱。规模相对较小，也不会覆盖所有飞机，但你能看出想坐头等舱的绝不仅仅是沿海地区，而是所有人。我认为面对头等舱客群结构的新趋势，American的枢纽表现完全没问题。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Hold on, hold on, because you kind of glaze over Allegiant, a small cabin on a small subfleet. But yeah, they have eight first-class seats.
transcript.zh: 等一下，等一下。你刚才把Allegiant的情况一笔带过了，那只是在一个小规模子机队上搞的小机舱。不过没错，他们有8个头等舱座位。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I'm not saying people in the flyover states don't want to fly in first class. Of course they do. And there's opportunity now that the way first-class pricing has changed over the years, you can buy up into that, and that's great. I'm just saying that 24 sounds like a lot of seats.
transcript.zh: 我不是说“飞越州”的人不想坐头等舱，他们当然想。而且随着这些年头等舱定价机制的转变，升舱加购变得很划算，这很好。我只是觉得24个座位听起来实在太多了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Okay, but Allegiant is an ultra-low-cost carrier. I mean, this is an airline that probably should have zero first-class seats. If they say there's room for eight, I think that there's probably room for 24.
transcript.zh: 好吧，但Allegiant可是一家ULCC（超低成本航司）。这种航司本来应该一个头等舱座位都没有的。如果他们都觉得容得下8个座，那我认为容纳24个座也完全合情合理。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, I think we're just quibbling over numbers at this point.
transcript.zh: 好吧，我觉得我们现在纯粹是在拿数字抬杠。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I think we are. So another copycat thing that American has done, and this is kind of both shocking and not shocking at all, screens. Screens are coming back fleet-wide, narrowbodies? Did you ever think you would see such a day, Brett?
transcript.zh: 确实如此。那么American跟风效仿的另一件事——这既令人震惊，又完全在意料之中——那就是屏幕。窄体机全机队要重新装回个人屏幕了？你曾想过能等到这一天吗，Brett？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, I did. But I figured it'd be under a different CEO. So...
transcript.zh: 想过啊，但我以为那得是换了新CEO之后的事了。所以嘛……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: People will do anything to keep their jobs, won't they?
transcript.zh: 人为了保住饭碗真是啥都肯干，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Apparently, yeah. I mean, look, screens have been hanging over this airline for such a long time. I mean American, you know, under United's current leadership team, plus Doug Parker, American got rid of the screens in the narrowbodies.
transcript.zh: 显然是的。你看，屏幕问题困扰这家航司实在太久了。我是说，在United现任领导班子——再加上Doug Parker的领导时期，American移除了窄体机上的屏幕。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And this was very much that US Airways mentality where cost was kind of the number one concern, and if you have fast Wi-Fi and streaming content, then...
transcript.zh: 这很大程度上是US Airways的心态作祟，成本被视作头号关注点。他们觉得只要有高速Wi-Fi和流媒体内容，那么……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: "Why do you need a screen? It just is expensive and doesn't do anything."
transcript.zh: “为什么一定要屏幕？又贵又没实质用处。”

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: This was a very reasonable argument. I just flew 11 and a half hours back from Copenhagen, and I never turned on the IFE once.
transcript.zh: 这确实曾是个非常站得住脚的论点。我刚从哥本哈根飞了11个半小时回来，机上娱乐系统（IFE）我一眼都没碰过。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I had brought my own content, things that I wanted to watch. And sadly, this airplane had no internet, which really stunk. But had say, Starlink been installed, the flight would have been a complete breeze.
transcript.zh: 我自己带了想看的内容。可惜这架飞机没有网络，体验确实很差。但如果装了像星链（Starlink）这样的网络，那这趟飞行就绝对会轻松惬意。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Uh no, no, Breeze uses Viasat. Sorry.
transcript.zh: 呃不是，微风航空（Breeze）用的是 Viasat。不好意思玩了个烂梗。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Oh, did I miss your jokes, Brett. You don't sound convincing.
transcript.zh: 哦，Brett，我可真“想念”你的冷笑话。听着一点都不好笑。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Anyway, with the old technology when American made this decision, I really thought it made some sense. The screens were heavy, and they've always gotten out of date within a few years. People are buying iPads much more often. It tends to be, at least for me, a better viewing experience.
transcript.zh: 总之，以当年的技术水准来看，当 American 做出这个决定时，我真觉得挺合理的。屏幕很重，而且过个几年就落伍淘汰了。大家换 iPad 的频率要高得多，而且至少对我来说，看 iPad 的视觉体验往往更好。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But the market saw it otherwise. Delta and United started calling themselves premium, and they were pointing to screens as a reason they had an advantage, and then they started making more revenue.
transcript.zh: 但市场给出了截然相反的答案。Delta 和 United 开始将自己标榜为高端航司，并把客舱屏幕列为自身优势之一，随后他们的营收便开始水涨船高。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I've had some interesting conversations with people in the industry about why the screens have been so successful. The easy answer would be that people go out of their way to buy tickets on airplanes that they know have screens because, you know, they want to watch them. I'm sure some people do that.
transcript.zh: 我和业内人士就“为什么屏幕策略如此成功”做过几次有趣的交流。显而易见的答案是，旅客会特地去买那些配备屏幕的航班机票，因为他们确实想看。我相信确实有部分人是出于这个原因。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But I think the other answer is more interesting. It's that screens are a way, in shorthand, to show passengers that the airline cares about them and the passenger experience.
transcript.zh: 但我认为另一个解释更有意思。屏幕其实是一种直观的代号，向旅客传递出航司重视他们以及乘机体验的信号。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So people get onto an airplane, they see the screens, particularly the newer screens with HD and the bright colors, and their brains register the cabin as having a better experience even if they never watch them.
transcript.zh: 所以当旅客登机后看到屏幕，尤其是那些色彩鲜艳的高清新款屏幕，哪怕他们根本不看，潜意识里也会觉得这间客舱的体验更好。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So in this case, the screens are kind of like that branding on the bulkhead wall or the ceiling tiles that are an option on the A320 series, but American has not invested in them. Are they needed? Do they really change the experience? No. Do they convey something premium? Absolutely.
transcript.zh: 所以从这个角度说，屏幕有点像舱壁上的品牌标识，或是 A320 系列上可选配但 American 没花钱买的天花板造型格栅。这些东西是必需的吗？能实质改变体验吗？并不能。但它们是否传达出高端感？绝对是的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And my major issue here is not that American decided not to have screens 10 years ago. It's that they saw where the industry was going, they saw that they had a disadvantage, and they waited so long to reverse course.
transcript.zh: 我最大的不满并不在于 American 十年前决定不装屏幕，而是在于他们明明看清了行业大势，也明白自己处于劣势，却硬是拖了这么久才掉头纠偏。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, the screen thing for me, it is something I have absolutely flip-flopped on over the years. And you can see it every time I've written about it on Cranky Flier.
transcript.zh: 没错，关于屏幕这件事，这些年来我自己的态度也完全翻转过。从我在 Cranky Flier 上写的那些文章就能看得清清楚楚。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I was originally more on team US Airways with this. Look, I was also wowed by device holders and Wi-Fi and all that kind of stuff, but I keep changing my mind.
transcript.zh: 我最初在这件事上是完全支持老全美航空（US Airways）那套逻辑的。你看，我也曾被自带设备支架、车载 Wi-Fi 之类的东西惊艳过，但我总在不断动摇。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Some of it would come from an actual experience. I'd be sitting on these airplanes, and I'd put my phone up to watch something, and then I'm trying to do work on my laptop. But then I need like a stupid two-factor code to log in from my phone, so I have to interrupt what I'm watching and do this.
transcript.zh: 这很大程度上来自于实际乘机体验。我坐在飞机上，把手机架起来看视频，同时又想在笔记本电脑上干活。结果我登录电脑需要手机上的双重身份验证码，我就不得不中断正在看的内容去操作手机。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And that's just annoying. And also, if you have screens, you can get newer content as well, just the way that these deals work. So the content's more interesting.
transcript.zh: 那确实挺烦人的。而且如果你有屏幕，按照版权交易的模式，你还能拿到更新的内容。所以内容本身也会更有吸引力。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And that, you know, combined with the aesthetic piece that you were talking about, it's less tangible. It's harder to put on a spreadsheet, which is probably why American didn't go in this direction for so long.
transcript.zh: 再加上你刚才提到的客舱视觉美感，这些虽然比较抽象、很难用财务电子表格去量化，这大概也是美国航空这么长时间以来一直没走这条路的原因。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But it really does give you that more premium feeling. It does make a big difference.
transcript.zh: 但它确实能给你一种更高端的品质感，带来的体验差异是非常显著的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Now, Brett, it might be easier to model on a spreadsheet now. These screens historically have just been a straight cost. I don't think that that has changed yet.
transcript.zh: 不过 Brett，现在要用财务模型量化它可能更容易了。以往这些屏幕纯粹就是一项硬性成本。我觉得这种情况目前虽然还没变，

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But we hear United and Delta talk about using these screens, monetizing these screens, so that they know who's sitting in the seat, what they like, what they don't like, and then serving them advertising based on that.
transcript.zh: 但我们看到美联航和达美航空都在探讨如何利用屏幕并实现屏幕变现。他们掌握了座上旅客的身份、喜好和厌恶，从而针对性地投放个性化广告。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That's kind of the holy grail. I don't think any airline does it the right way yet, but if they can get there, maybe the screens can make some money for them.
transcript.zh: 这算是终极商业蓝图。我觉得目前还没有哪家航司真正做成，但如果能实现，屏幕或许真能帮他们赚到钱。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, I'm a believer in that. I think it's coming. I mean, it's already there, we just, I don't know, they haven't revved the engine yet, right?
transcript.zh: 是的，我对此深信不疑。我认为这一天迟早会来。或者说基础其实已经具备了，只是他们还没把引擎油门踩到底，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And we can look at American to see this opportunity. Former Chief Commercial Officer Vasu Raja, after he was gone from American, he bought a data company and then ended up now temporarily running United's in-house Kinective ad network, which is meant to monetize those screens.
transcript.zh: 而且我们可以从美航身上看到这个商机。美航前任首席商务官 Vasu Raja 离职后，收购了一家数据公司，现在暂时接管了美联航自建的 Kinective 广告网络，其核心目的就是为了将那些屏幕变现。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So Vasu must have known this opportunity at American. It's not like all of a sudden he left and was like, "Oh, maybe this is a good idea," right? But when he was at American, he didn't have any screens to work with on the narrowbodies, so he had to look elsewhere for revenue growth opportunities when he was there.
transcript.zh: 所以 Vasu 当初在美航时肯定就看出了这块机会。总不可能他一离职就突然顿悟觉得这是个好主意吧？但在美航期间，他的窄体机机队上根本没有任何屏幕可用，所以当时他只能去其他地方寻找收入增长点。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So, Brett, American is going to get this option eventually to monetize the screens. The problem with the screens is that it's going to take forever to install them.
transcript.zh: 所以 Brett，美航最终也会拥有将屏幕变现的筹码。但屏幕最大的问题在于，安装改装需要耗费极其漫长的时间。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And I don't think this is necessarily an American-specific problem. You know, you can get new Wi-Fi, like American is doing with Starlink on some planes, and you can flip that switch relatively quickly. Screens just take a very long time to install fleet-wide. It's going to be a multi-year process.
transcript.zh: 我觉得这倒不一定是美航独有的问题。机上 Wi-Fi 比如美航部分客机选装的星链系统，相对而言可以很快切换上线。但要在全机队安装客舱屏幕则极其耗时，注定会是一个跨越数年的大工程。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And apparently, Brett, this is not even starting until 2028?
transcript.zh: 而且显然，Brett，这项工程甚至要等到 2028 年才会真正启动？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, and this is kind of the broader issue at American, right? It's that they need more urgency in what they're doing. And I agree with you, we talked about this earlier, what was it, 160,000 seats, I said, in the narrowbody fleet? That is a lot of screens you have to put on there.
transcript.zh: 没错，而这恰恰暴露了美航更深层的问题，对吧？他们在推进行动上缺乏足够的紧迫感。我很赞同你的看法，我们之前提到过，美航窄体机机队大概有多少个座位来着？我记得我说的是 16 万个座位吧？那可是要加装天文数字般的屏幕量。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But deliveries won't start until 2028, and it's going to take into the early part of the 2030s to get it done. That's a lifetime at this point.
transcript.zh: 但新交付机型要到 2028 年才开始配备，而全机队完成改装得一路拖到 2030 年代初。在当前这个时代，这漫长得就像一个世纪。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And it's a little poetic that this announcement was made just as the very last of the narrowbodies, the handful of A319s, went into the maintenance shop to have their screens removed. So this is a blank slate. But...
transcript.zh: 而且颇具讽刺意味的是，就在这项决策宣布的同时，美航窄体机中仅存的最后几架装有屏幕的 A319，刚好进机库 MRO 车间拆除了客舱屏幕。所以他们现在完全是一张白纸重新来过。但是……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: This is one thing that, yes, it is very difficult to do, and it takes a long time. But then there's other things, I mean, you talk about Starlink, which is only on some of the fleet. We'll get into this later, but how the organizational changes—there needs to be more urgency. This is better than it was, but it's not where it needs to be.
transcript.zh: 改造确实非常困难，而且耗时漫长。但还有其他方面，比如你提到的星链，目前只覆盖了部分机队。我们稍后会深入探讨组织架构调整，但必须有更强的紧迫感。现状确实比过去好，但还远远没达到应有的水平。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: There does need to be more urgency. I hope to see it. Let me just finish this part of the show by at least giving American some credit. We had that multi-part series of 'What's wrong with American?' We pointed out several of these things. Look, American is making a strategy change.
transcript.zh: 确实需要更强的紧迫感，我也希望能看到。在结束这部分讨论前，我至少要给美航一些肯定。我们之前做过'美航到底怎么了'的多期系列专题，指出了其中不少问题。看，美航现在正在调整战略。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And it does deserve to be commended for at least finally realizing that something was wrong and changing course. Is that the most positive thing I've ever said about American Airlines?
transcript.zh: 他们终于意识到出了问题并调整航向，这确实值得称赞。这算不算我评价美国航空时说过最客气的话了？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It might be. And it is earned, but, you know, it's also we just need to play catch-up now. They've lost so much time that there's nothing I'm seeing that says, 'Hey, we're innovating, we're making huge, amazing, important changes.'
transcript.zh: 可能真是。这是他们应得的，但说到底，他们现在只是在努力补课。他们浪费了太多时间，目前我看不到任何迹象表明：'我们在创新，在推行颠覆性、重大的变革。'

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It's we're still trying to play catch-up. And by the time they're done playing catch-up, where will Delta and United be? And that's the hard part when you've lost all this time.
transcript.zh: 他们依然在疲于追赶。而等到他们补齐短板时，达美和美联航又会走到哪一步？这就是浪费大把光阴后不得不面对的残酷现实。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It is the hard part. We talked a lot about product in the first part of the show. Let's take a break now, and when we return, maybe we can talk about the recent organizational changes at the airline.
transcript.zh: 确实很难。前半段节目我们聊了很多机上硬件与客舱产品。现在我们先插播一段广告，休息回来后，我们来聊聊美航近期的高管人事与组织架构变动。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I want to ask you about two travelers I think airlines quietly struggle with: the person who just doesn't care about loyalty programs, and the one that is not ready for a co-branded credit card.
transcript.zh: 我想问你关于航司私底下最头疼的两类旅客：一类是根本不在乎常旅客计划的人，另一类是还没准备好办联名信用卡的人。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Oh, I know these people. The first one books whatever is most convenient or cheapest, and has no built-in loyalty. And the other one is loyal, but doesn't want another credit card.
transcript.zh: 噢，我太了解这两种人了。第一类旅客只买最方便或最便宜的票，毫无品牌忠诚度可言；另一类旅客虽然认可品牌，但不想再办一张信用卡。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: This is a problem for airlines, and that's why Flex Pay works hand in hand with them to address both of these gaps and help them acquire new customers and grow loyalty.
transcript.zh: 这正是航司面临的痛点，因此 Flex Pay 与航司紧密合作，直击这两大缺口，助力航司获客并培育旅客忠诚度。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So I know Flex Pay as a payment option, but it's also an on-ramp to the loyalty highway?
transcript.zh: 我一直以为 Flex Pay 只是一种支付方式，难道它还能作为通往常旅客体系快车道的引流入口？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That's a good way to describe it. Flex Pay helps airlines give customers products that build loyalty over time, that are not directly tied to their currency.
transcript.zh: 这个比喻很贴切。Flex Pay 协助航司向客户提供能逐步沉淀忠诚度的产品，且无需直接与航司积分货币挂钩。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So the airline isn't losing that customer, and in many cases, they're nurturing them into loyal travelers on a much faster timeline, even before they get a credit card. But how does Flex Pay make that happen?
transcript.zh: 这么说航司不仅没有流失这些客户，反而在许多情况下能以更快的节奏将他们转化为忠诚旅客，甚至在他们办联名卡之前就完成转化。但 Flex Pay 具体是如何做到的呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Glad you asked. Flex Pay provides the convenience and flexibility of paying monthly for travel purchases, and that data shows that Flex Pay users have really high repeat booking rates. It keeps them coming back to the same airline.
transcript.zh: 问得好。Flex Pay 针对旅行支出提供便捷、灵活的分期按月付款服务；数据显示，Flex Pay 用户的复购率极高，能有效促使他们持续选择同一家航司。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So the product itself becomes the loyalty driver for those who may not be as drawn to points as others are?
transcript.zh: 所以对于那些对常旅客积分不太感冒的人来说，这种支付产品本身就成了培育忠诚度的抓手？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yep, and airlines should view it that way. Flex Pay isn't just a payment option, it's a way to create a relationship with customers who would otherwise be completely transactional. Flex Pay also offers loyalty auto-enroll, so those...
transcript.zh: 没错，航司也正应该这样看待它。Flex Pay 不仅仅是一种支付手段，更是与那些原本纯做'一锤子买卖'的客群建立深度黏性的方式。此外，Flex Pay 还支持常旅客自动注册，让那些……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: customers can start earning points immediately, kick-starting their loyalty journey in more ways than one. That's a pretty compelling case for a customer segment that most loyalty programs just write off.
transcript.zh: 客户可以立即开始赚取积分，以多种方式开启他们的忠诚度之旅。对于大多数常旅客计划直接放弃的客群而言，这确实很有说服力。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And that's exactly why airlines are paying attention to it. This is sponsored by Upgrade, Inc. Learn more at upgrade.com/flex-pay.
transcript.zh: 这也正是航空公司开始关注这一领域的原因。本期节目由 Upgrade, Inc. 赞助播出。欲了解更多信息，请访问 upgrade.com/flex-pay。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And we're back. Let's talk about the org chart, Brett. I've been a little harsh in recent years about American's communication strategy, which I might summarize as, "We deflect everything, and then we hope it will go away." Then it doesn't.
transcript.zh: 欢迎回来。Brett，我们来聊聊组织架构图。这几年我对美国航空的公关传播策略批评得有点狠，我可以将其总结为：“我们避重就轻、推诿一切，然后指望问题能自行消失。”但问题往往并没有消失。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I can't say that I was surprised to see the highest-level departure earlier this month, and that's Ron DeFeo, Executive Vice President and Chief Communications Officer. Brett, do you know my biggest problem with Ron?
transcript.zh: 本月早些时候看到最高级别的离职变动，我一点也不感到意外——那就是执行副总裁兼首席传播官 Ron DeFeo 的离开。Brett，你知道我对 Ron 最大的不满是什么吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Tell me why.
transcript.zh: 快跟我说说为什么？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That's actually the greatest joke that you've ever made. Not that many people are going to get it, but those that do are really going to enjoy it. But let me tell you why.
transcript.zh: 这其实是你讲过最绝的段子。虽然能听懂的人可能不多，但听懂的人肯定会拍案叫绝。不过还是让我来告诉你为什么吧。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: With all the stuff I wrote and said about American's faults over the years—and I stand by I think all of it—Ron never got outwardly angry with me. He was always very nice to me when we spoke in person.
transcript.zh: 这些年来我写过、说过那么多关于美国航空的各种过失——而且我认为所有的批评我都坚持到底——但 Ron 从未对我公然发火。我们当面交谈时，他对我一直都非常客气。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You talked to him?
transcript.zh: 你居然跟他聊过？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, maybe I'm old school, but I like a good old-fashioned shouting match with a comms person every now and then, or at least maybe some trading of passive-aggressive emails.
transcript.zh: Brett，也许我比较老派吧，但我挺喜欢偶尔和公关负责人来一场老派的激烈争吵，或者至少来回发几封冷嘲热讽的邮件。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I really got a chance to do both of those things during the United Jeff Smisek years. In fact, I kept some of those emails. The thing was, Ron was very, very even, and I found that to be weird.
transcript.zh: 在美联航 Jeff Smisek 执掌的时期，这两样我都结结实实经历过，甚至我还保留了其中一些邮件。问题就在于，Ron 的情绪实在太稳定了，让我觉得非常不可思议。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But anyways, I hear he's very happy now. Whether it was his choice to go or not, it seems like he's content with his decision. Lots of stress in that job.
transcript.zh: 但不管怎样，我听说他现在过得很开心。无论离职是否完全出于自愿，他似乎对自己的决定都挺满意的。毕竟那份工作的压力确实太大了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, no question about that. I mean, could you imagine trying to run comms for American over the last decade? That sounds exhausting just thinking about it.
transcript.zh: 噢，那毫无疑问。我是说，你能想象过去十年里掌管美国航空的公关部是种什么体验吗？光是想想都觉得精疲力竭。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But also, Ron did more than just comms, and his empire is now being dismantled. His number two, Caroline Clayton, she will step into the role leading comms.
transcript.zh: 而且，Ron 管的可不仅仅是公关，他的权力版图如今正在被拆分。他的二把手 Caroline Clayton 将接任主管公关事务。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But she was also running marketing under him, and that is now going to a undisclosed new hire in the commercial group under Chief Commercial Officer, Nat Pieper.
transcript.zh: 但她此前在他手下还兼管市场营销，而该业务现在将划归商务部门，由首席商务官 Nat Pieper 麾下一位尚未公布的新聘高管接管。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Then Ron also has some weird HR-related functions, so those are going to move over there to the HR team or People, as they like to call it, and pretend it's not just HR.
transcript.zh: 此外 Ron 还管过一些奇奇怪怪的人力资源职能，这些业务也将移交给 HR 团队——或者像他们喜欢的那样称之为“人才管理部”（People），装作这不仅仅是 HR 似的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, but at least they don't capitalize it in every press release.
transcript.zh: 是啊，但至少他们不会在每篇新闻通稿里都大写特写。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That is a great point. That's a different part of the metroplex, I believe. Meanwhile, over in the finance world, not much changes there, so this is really not about that.
transcript.zh: 说得太对了。据我所知那是达拉斯-沃斯堡大都会区另一家航司的作风。与此同时，在财务条线方面，并没有太大变动，所以这次调整其实与财务无关。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Devon May still CFO. The only...
transcript.zh: Devon May 仍然担任 CFO。唯一的……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Change with him is that he will now take corporate real estate under his wing. And this is because the person who used to do that was Nate Gatten. Nate had three very weird departments in one place. Besides corporate real estate, he had Government Affairs and American Eagle.
transcript.zh: 关于他的变动是，他现在将把企业不动产业务收归麾下。这是因为之前负责这块的是 Nate Gatten。Nate 手下当时管着三个风马牛不相及的部门，除了企业不动产，他还管政府事务和美鹰航空。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, a strange combination. But I know that Nate was very well thought of and I feel like at the highest levels of these airlines, if you're going to be an EVP, you have to have more than one portfolio, so they gave him some other stuff.
transcript.zh: 是啊，挺奇怪的组合。但我知道大家对 Nate 评价很高，而且我觉得在这些航司的最高管理层，如果你是个执行副总裁，手头总得管不止一块业务，所以他们就塞给了他一些别的东西。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I guess. But there's a lot in American's org chart that's weird like this. I'm guessing it made sense to someone at some point just for this individual person, but they were kind of letting the people tailor the organization to what was needed.
transcript.zh: 也许吧。但美航的组织架构图里有很多诸如此类的奇葩设置。我猜可能在某个时期，针对某个具体的人确实说得通，但他们有点像是因人设岗，让组织去迎合具体的人的需求。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And now that those people are leaving or had already left, now they can try and smooth this out, which is how this all really just generally feels to me. But anyway, Nate's off to sunnier pastures. He is heading to do government affairs for Apple, which means he is about to be a whole lot richer.
transcript.zh: 现在这些人要离职或者已经离开了，他们终于可以着手理顺这些关系了。这基本就是整件事给我的感觉。不过不管怎样，Nate 是奔向更好的前程了，他要去苹果公司负责政府事务，这意味着他马上要发大财了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And his SVP of Government Affairs will now take over, and then American Eagle will be pushed into the operation under COO David Seymour.
transcript.zh: 而他手下负责政府事务的高级副总裁现在将接棒，然后美鹰航空将被划归到首席运营官 David Seymour 负责的运营板块。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Let's talk more about the operation, which has been suffering a little bit. There were some changes there as well, right?
transcript.zh: 我们多聊聊运营层面吧，美航的运营最近表现一直不太尽如人意。那边也有一些人事变动，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, it was there in the commercial side that had the biggest changes. So on the ops side, the head of Tech Ops, Kevin Brickner, is retiring, whether that's really retiring or not, we don't know, and they have hired John Bendoraitis, better known as Bendo, to take his place.
transcript.zh: 对，运营和商业板块的变化是最大的。在运营端，技术运营负责人 Kevin Brickner 即将退休——究竟是不是真的退休我们不得而知——他们聘请了 John Bendoraitis，大家更熟悉叫他 Bendo，来接替他的职位。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So Bendo was the COO at Spirit until Spirit stopped having an O, I guess. So Bendo, new hire, good for him.
transcript.zh: Bendo 之前是精神航空的首席运营官，直到精神航空彻底玩不转运营了为止吧。所以 Bendo 作为新进高管，挺替他高兴的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There's also JC Gulbranson, who is currently SVP of Flight Ops and IOC, which is the operation center. He is now going to also take on airport operations and operations planning. So those are two roles that used to report directly to David Seymour, who is still in charge.
transcript.zh: 还有 JC Gulbranson，他目前是负责飞行运行和一体化运行中心（IOC，即运行中心）的高级副总裁。他现在还将接管机场地面运营和运行规划。这两个职位过去都是直接向 David Seymour 汇报的，David 目前依然大权在握。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But I have heard from multiple people that maybe that won't be the case for much longer, it may be time for a retirement plan there. Just a matter of when that's going to happen. So that would suggest to me that JC is the heir apparent unless Bendo impresses quickly when he gets there, I guess.
transcript.zh: 但我听不止一个人说，这种情况可能不会持续太久了，可能快到制定退休计划的时候了，只是时间早晚的问题。所以这在我看来意味着 JC 就是预定的接班人，除非 Bendo 入职后能迅速拿出惊艳的表现。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So does all of this show that Robert Isom is finally grasping the urgency of this and making bold decisions about his team?
transcript.zh: 那么这一切是否说明，Robert Isom 终于意识到事情的紧迫性，开始对自己的团队痛下决心、大刀阔斧地做决策了？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No, maybe. I don't really have an answer for you. The operation has been running poorly on and off for such a long time, and it's the same people that have been running it.
transcript.zh: 不是，也许吧，我真给不出确切答案。美航的运行断断续续拉胯这么长时间了，而且一直是同一拨人在管。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So okay, now we've got Tech Ops under new blood. But they're spinning this as Kevin Brickner is retiring and that David Seymour actually asked him to...
transcript.zh: 好吧，现在技术运营引进了新鲜血液。但他们对外宣称是 Kevin Brickner 正常退休，而且 David Seymour 实际上还挽留他……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: stay around longer than he wanted. Which is just, like this whole round of changes, the comms folks that I talked to, they tried to make it clear that everybody left on their own.
transcript.zh: 待的时间超过了他的预期。这整轮人事变动，跟我聊过的公关人员都极力表明所有人都是主动离职的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And I think this is nuts. Like, if Robert is trying to show that he is a change leader making these bold moves and fixing everything, then he should be saying he's firing people. And I know you can't do that once you hit a certain level, no one gets fired once you're at that level.
transcript.zh: 我觉得这简直不可理喻。如果 Robert 想要展现自己是一个推动变革的领袖，采取大胆行动解决所有问题，那他就应该挑明是他解雇了这些人。我知道到了高管级别不能这么做，到了那个级别没人会被公开“解雇”。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But instead, they just act like this is a reaction to people leaving on their own, which is decidedly less inspiring, right? This is not going to really rally people here.
transcript.zh: 但相反，他们表现得好像这只是对员工主动离职的应对，这显然太缺乏号召力了，对吧？这根本不可能振奋人心。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, you know, Brett, they don't even try to spin me anymore. Nobody calls and pretends anything to me. I just read the press releases or whatever.
transcript.zh: 你懂的，Brett，他们现在甚至都懒得来公关我了。没人打电话给我演戏，我直接看新闻通稿完事。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, I called them. I reached out to them. Okay. But, you know, you can read it, and you can make decisions on what you think is happening here and what you think is not.
transcript.zh: 我是主动打电话找他们的。行吧。但你看完这些，完全可以自行判断哪些是真的在发生，哪些不是。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But if the spin is, "No, this is just we're trying to fix everything, and, you know, clean up some of the issues and make it right, but everyone left on their own," like, what does that say about Robert's urgency here?
transcript.zh: 如果他们的公关说辞是：“不，这只是我们在努力拨乱反正、解决部分问题并走回正轨，而且大家都是主动离开的”——那这能体现出 Robert 所谓的紧迫感吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, the only guy to truly get fired there was Vasu, right?
transcript.zh: 美航真正被开掉的就只有 Vasu 一个人，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That was, yeah, I don't even know that they even said that, but that was pretty clear what was happening.
transcript.zh: 确实，我都不知道他们有没有明说，但大家心里都很清楚是怎么回事。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I just don't know what to say about Robert anymore. I don't think this is going to do it. I still think it's only a matter of time until he retires. I just don't know what that time is.
transcript.zh: 关于 Robert，我真的无话可说了。我觉得这根本起不到作用。我依然认为他“退休”只是时间问题，我只是不知道具体是什么时候。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That was a "retires" in quotes there for you?
transcript.zh: 你说的这个“退休”是打引号的吧？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Look, the guy will have spent how many decades at American and its predecessor companies? He will be in his 60s. You know, that's kind of retiring, isn't it?
transcript.zh: 你想想，这家伙在美航及其前身公司待了多少个十年？他也快六十多岁了。到那个时候，这也算得上退休了吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Not clear if it's by choice. Well, it's by someone's choice. It's not clear whose choice.
transcript.zh: 说不清是不是自愿的。好吧，反正是某人的选择，只是不知道是谁的选择罢了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But, okay, let's talk about the commercial side because this is sort of a different animal here. The commercial side is the one group that has a new leader, and new to the airline, right?
transcript.zh: 不过好吧，我们来聊聊商业业务板块，因为这完全是另一码事。商业板块是唯一一个迎来新负责人的团队，而且对这家航司来说也是个新人，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So we have Nat Pieper, Chief Commercial Officer, has not been there a year yet. Came from Oneworld. He was at Alaska, before that he was at Delta and Northwest before that.
transcript.zh: 首席商务官 Nat Pieper 上任还不足一年。他来自寰宇一家（Oneworld），此前在阿拉斯加航空工作，更早之前还在达美航空和西北航空任职。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So Nat, I had expected maybe we'd see some changes when he took over, like bigger organizational changes, but we haven't seen that yet. And so now I'm wondering if, with what's happened now, now that the organization has been more settled, maybe he can make more changes.
transcript.zh: 所以我原本以为 Nat 上任时我们能看到一些变革，比如更大的组织架构调整，但目前为止还没看到。现在我在想，随着如今的变动尘埃落定、组织更加稳定，他或许可以推行更多变革了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So what did he do? Okay. He takes over the entire customer organization. So Heather Garboden is the Chief Customer Officer, which is silly because she's a chief reporting to another chief, which always drives me nuts with the title inflation stuff. But her job is very important.
transcript.zh: 那他到底做了什么呢？好的。他接管了整个客户组织架构。Heather Garboden 担任首席客户官，这其实挺搞笑的，因为一个 Chief 要向另一个 Chief 汇报，这种头衔通胀总让我抓狂。不过她的职责确实至关重要。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And in her job, she used to have a split reporting role where she went to both commercial and the operation, which is terrible. I don't care what they say, I hate having to serve two masters. That is brutal.
transcript.zh: 而在她的岗位上，她以前需要同时向商务和运行双线汇报，这简直糟透了。不管别人怎么说，我最讨厌同时侍奉两个老板，那太痛苦了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So now she is fully in Nat's organization out of the operation. And she has also taken reservations, contact center, service recovery, and catering with her, away
transcript.zh: 所以现在她彻底脱离了运行部门，完全归入 Nat 的团队。并且她还把订座预付、客服联络中心、服务补救以及机上餐饮等业务也一并带走了，不再归运行管辖。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: From the operational side, it now reports up into her. That's good. So now will we start seeing Nat make more changes? And maybe he already has, right? He's the guy who probably convinced Robert to put the screens back in and, you know, some of the catering changes and things like that. We've certainly seen change.
transcript.zh: 从运行端来看，现在也归她管辖了。这挺好的。那接下来我们会看到 Nat 推动更多变革吗？也许他已经这么做了，对吧？很可能就是他说服了 Robert 重新装回机上屏幕，还对餐饮等环节做了改进。我们确实看到了转变。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But I want to see what else is coming. This feels like kind of settling his domain a little bit here. So with all those changes, it feels like Nat's group is growing in influence, which is that new blood we had talked about. And it makes sense, because if you are Robert, you want to convince people that you've reinvented yourself, and you're a true believer in the premium world and all this.
transcript.zh: 但我还想看看后续会有什么动作。这感觉像是在进一步稳固他的势力范围。伴随着这些变动，Nat 的团队影响力似乎在不断扩大，这正是我们之前聊到的“新鲜血液”。这很合理，因为如果你是 Robert，你想让大家相信你已经洗心革面，成了高端出行理念的忠实拥趸。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So everyone else in the company has been there for so long. You need to make moves to get that new blood to have more power. So that is what this feels like, trying to sort of untangle some of the issues and shift the power a little bit.
transcript.zh: 公司里的其他人资历都太深了。你必须采取行动，让这股新鲜血液掌握更大的权力。所以目前的动作给人的感觉就是：尝试梳理现存的一些顽疾，并对权力格局进行微调。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, I've heard a lot of good things about Nat from people at American: that he actually cares, that he interacts with employees, that he speaks with the frontline. All this stuff shouldn't be surprising; it's what airline executives do all over the industry.
transcript.zh: Brett，我从美航内部员工那里听到了很多关于 Nat 的好评：说他真心投入、走近员工，并且乐于跟一线员工沟通。这些其实本不该让人大惊小怪，全行业的航司高管大多都这么做。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But I feel like as Robert has been embattled, he's like gone into a bunker at the Skyview headquarters and he hasn't come out. And it's nice to see somebody like Nat take the problems at American seriously, and interact with people, and just be available. I don't know that he can fix everything, but it's a good change of pace for American.
transcript.zh: 但我觉得，随着 Robert 深陷内外交困的境地，他仿佛把自己关进了 Skyview 总部的地堡里闭门不出。看到 Nat 这样的人能认真对待美航的问题、与大家互动交流、随时保持沟通姿态，确实令人欣慰。我不指望他能解决所有难题，但对美航而言，这无疑是一股新气象。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I would agree with that. And I think it's still really tough, right? I mean, if you're Nat, you want to try and do all this stuff, but you're not the CEO. And whether they think at the board level that he's ready to be CEO or not, who knows? But you would assume that with the airline going in this direction, if they're looking at an internal candidate, it's probably Nat, because there's not really anyone else that would seem to fit in this premium type of focus.
transcript.zh: 我同意。但我觉得这依然非常棘手，对吧？我是说，如果你是 Nat，你一心想大展身手推进这些事，但你终究不是 CEO。至于董事会层面试否认为他已经做好了接任 CEO 的准备，谁也说不准。不过可以预见，随着航司朝这个方向推进，如果他们考虑内部人选，大概率就是 Nat 了，因为似乎没有其他高管更契合这种发力高端的定位。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But, you know, he's not that CEO. Robert is the CEO, and so you're still working in this sort of weird box that it makes it challenging, I think, to engage the frontline as well. Did you see the memo that went to the officers when they made these changes?
transcript.zh: 但事实是，他现在还不是 CEO。Robert 才是 CEO，所以你依然处在某种微妙的条条框框之下，我认为这也给发动一线员工带来了挑战。公布这些变动时发给高级管理人员的那份备忘录，你看了吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I was cleaning up barf in the Serengeti, but I vaguely remember somebody sending it to me.
transcript.zh: 我当时正在塞伦盖蒂收拾呕吐物呢，不过我隐约记得有人把备忘录转给我了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah. So, you know, Robert had a memo that went out to his officers, and of course it was going to leak, so if you're writing that, it had to be written with that in mind. But instead of being reassuring, it kind of did the opposite for me.
transcript.zh: 对。Robert 给他的高管团队发了一份备忘录，这种文件必然会泄露，所以起草时肯定预先考虑到了这一点。但这份备忘录非但没起到安抚人心的作用，反而让我有了适得其反的感觉。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Because you have a guy who's been at the top for a really long time, things have not been going well, changes need to be made. This is a big change, and he is trying to shift how he talks about all this stuff. But this change on its own is still going to throw people for a loop.
transcript.zh: 因为你面对的是一位久居高位的一把手，当前局面很不理想，亟需作出改变。这次人事调整动静很大，他也试图改变自己谈论这些问题的口径。但单就这项调整本身而言，依然会让大家感到措手不及。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: a loop, right? You have senior leaders leaving, you have things that are changing where they report in the company. There's a lot of change in there.
transcript.zh: 这种恶性循环，对吧？高管接连离职，公司内部的汇报线也在不断变动。内部确实发生了非常多的变化。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And you would think that if you're going to put memos out, that you want to be trying to calm that down. You want to try and calm down some of the chaos and the anxiety and all that.
transcript.zh: 按理说，如果要发布全员备忘录，理应是想借此稳定军心，尽量平息内部的一些混乱和焦虑情绪。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But instead, Robert said this, quote, "The first step in a series of actions designed to strengthen our team, foster greater alignment, and act with greater urgency across the enterprise," end quote.
transcript.zh: 但相反，Robert 却这样写道，我引用一下：“这是旨在加强我们团队实力、促进更紧密协同，并在全公司范围内以更高紧迫感采取行动的一系列举措的第一步。”引用完毕。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's good parallel structure.
transcript.zh: 这排比句写得挺工整啊。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I hate the corporate speak. I hate that it just leaves people hanging, and I hate that they're talking about acting with greater urgency while simultaneously slow-rolling changes into multiple tranches with all this uncertainty. It's just bad.
transcript.zh: 我真讨厌这种企业官话套话。我讨厌它让人心里悬着没底，更讨厌他们一边高喊着要以更强的紧迫感行动，一边又在充斥着不确定性的情况下，把各种变革分期分批地慢吞吞推进。这真的很糟糕。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And so, I think as good as Nat can be, maybe is, you're still kind of working in this tumultuous environment.
transcript.zh: 所以，我认为哪怕 Nat 再有能力，或者事实确实如此，你依然是在这样一个动荡不安的环境中艰难开展工作。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, I think that you're right there. I've been harping on American's communications approach for a very long time at this point. I think there's work to be done there.
transcript.zh: Brett，我觉得你这点说得没错。关于美航的沟通策略，我其实已经反复批评很久了。我认为他们在这方面确实还有很多功课要做。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But we have made it this far in the show and I still think that you've forgotten to discuss an important point about what we're seeing at American. I think that you did because you're too much of a network geek. Do you know what this is?
transcript.zh: 但我们节目都录到这儿了，我还是觉得你遗漏了一个关于美航现状的重要讨论点。我觉得你漏掉是因为你太沉迷于航线网络规划了。你知道我说的是什么吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, it must be the thing announced the day we record this that American will start handing out Goldfish as a snack. Is that what we're talking about?
transcript.zh: 噢，那肯定是我们录节目的今天刚宣布的那件事：美航要开始提供小金鱼饼干（Goldfish）当零食了。你说的是这个吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Wait, really? I missed that release. Are they actually handing out Goldfish?
transcript.zh: 等等，真的假的？我漏看这篇新闻稿了。他们真要发小金鱼饼干？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, that just came out this morning. Biscoffs in the morning, Goldfish and, I think, cookies in the afternoon. But, yeah, Goldfish for all.
transcript.zh: 对，今天早晨刚发的消息。早上发 Biscoff 焦糖饼干，下午发小金鱼饼干，好像还有曲奇。不过没错，人人都有小金鱼饼干吃。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So stick with me here. And I know that some of our listeners, the big airline nerds out here, probably aren't going to agree with me here. But this is actually a big deal, okay?
transcript.zh: 大家先听我说完。我知道有些听众，尤其是那些资深航司发烧友，可能不太赞同我的观点。但这实际上是一件大事，好吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Branded snacks, they are a thing, kind of like screens and branding on bulkhead walls and the tiles on the ceiling. You know, people tell me that if passengers recognize the brand on the package of pretzels that they're served, they view the airline as more premium.
transcript.zh: 品牌联名零食可不是小事，这就像机载个人屏幕、舱壁隔板上的品牌标识以及机舱顶部的贴面一样。很多人告诉我，如果乘客能在发给他们的椒盐脆饼包装袋上认出知名品牌，他们就会觉得这家航司更加高端。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And I think up until this point, the only branded snack American has served are Biscoffs. And I'm pretty sure that I've complained about this before, the lack of branded snacks.
transcript.zh: 而且我觉得在此之前，美航提供过的唯一品牌零食就只有 Biscoff。我敢肯定我以前就抱怨过这点，也就是缺乏有品牌的零食。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, listen, it's a new day for you. I'm just glad it's not Cheez-Its, cuz those suck and I'm on Team Goldfish.
transcript.zh: 行吧，听着，对你来说这是翻开新篇章了。我反正是挺庆幸不是发 Cheez-It 芝士饼干的，因为那玩意儿太难吃了，我绝对站小金鱼饼干这边。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, exciting stuff. Another step forward for American. But that was not what I was trying to get at. I wanted to talk briefly about marketing.
transcript.zh: 好吧，确实挺令人振奋，算是美航向前迈出的又一步。但这并不是我原本想说的重点。我想简单聊聊市场营销。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You mentioned it earlier, but American is getting a new chief marketing officer, probably somebody from the outside. And we mentioned how American EVPs have worn many hats. We said that Ron has led the marketing team, very nice guy, we mentioned.
transcript.zh: 你之前提到过，美航正在物色一位新的首席营销官（CMO），很可能会从外部空降。而且我们之前也说过美航的高级副总裁们身兼数职。我们提到过 Ron 此前一直兼管市场营销团队，我们也说过他为人非常好。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm not sure that Ron knew so much about marketing. That was not his background, and even if he cared deeply about it, I don't think there was any budget for marketing. The good news: I think American is going to take marketing seriously, and then this new marketing person not going to report to Comms anymore.
transcript.zh: 我不确定 Ron 对市场营销有多了解。那不是他的背景出身，而且就算他非常在乎，我觉得当时也没有任何营销预算。好消息是，我认为美航现在开始认真对待市场营销了，而且这位新任营销负责人不会再向公关部门汇报了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Just remember, okay, airlines aren't quite the commodity business that they used to be. But for the most part, a seat is still a seat. Most of these airlines use chairs from the same manufacturers, and people still choose an airline based on how it makes them feel. They want these brands to care about them.
transcript.zh: 但别忘了，现在的航司确实不像过去那样纯粹是同质化竞争的大宗商品。但在很大程度上，座位终归还是个座位。大多数航司采购的座椅都来自同一批制造商，旅客选择哪家航司，依然取决于航司带给他们的感觉。他们希望这些品牌是在乎自己的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm going to bet that many even non-aviation geeks remember, "Something special in the air"?
transcript.zh: 我敢打赌，很多甚至都不是航空迷的人，都会记得那句“空中非凡体验”（Something special in the air）吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: We're American Airlines, something special in the air.
transcript.zh: （哼唱）我们是美国航空，为您带来空中非凡体验……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Usually I hate it when you do that, but the jingle was so great, I'm glad you did it for the listeners. Brett, if you and I went to LAX now—and why would we do that, of course—and we asked 200 travelers if they've ever heard of, "Caring for people on life's journey," you think anybody would know what that is?
transcript.zh: 通常你这么唱我很受不了，但这广告曲实在太经典了，我很高兴你为听众唱了出来。Brett，要是咱俩现在去洛杉矶国际机场（LAX）——当然我们没事干嘛去那儿——去问 200 个旅客有没有听过“关怀人生旅程中的每一个人”（Caring for people on life's journey），你觉得有人会知道那是啥吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, if they've watched a safety video on American at some point, they might remember it.
transcript.zh: 有啊，要是他们曾在美航飞机上看安全须知视频时注意过的话，说不定能想起来。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I don't know. Marketing isn't going to fix American Airlines. But if they do fix the airline, marketing is going to let people know that something has changed. And I'm glad to see American investing in that.
transcript.zh: 我看悬。市场营销本身并不能拯救美航。但如果他们真把航司自身的问题解决了，营销就能让大家知道情况有了改变。我很高兴看到美航愿意在这方面做投入。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yes, but you have to actually fix the airline first. And I know there's this chicken-or-the-egg thing here: when can you start talking about it? But if you start telling people everything is great when your operation isn't, and you're still not quite there, you're just going to end up in a world of hurt.
transcript.zh: 是的，但你必须先切切实实把航司修整好。我知道这存在先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题：你到底该什么时候开始对外宣传？但如果你的运营根本没跟上、自己还没做到位，就到处跟人吹嘘一切都棒极了，最终只会自讨苦吃。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, it's not that, "Everything is great," it's that American is, "Going for great."
transcript.zh: Brett，这不是说“一切都棒极了”，而是美航正在“奔向卓越”（Going for great）。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, no. How many people you think would recognize that one? I hated that slogan so much. It just sounded so stupid.
transcript.zh: 天呐，打住。你觉得又有几个人认得这句？我当年讨厌死这句口号了，听起来实在太傻了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: World's greatest flyers fly American?
transcript.zh: “世界上最伟大的常飞旅客都乘美航”（World's greatest flyers fly American）这句呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: God, they really did have a lot of irrelevant slogans, didn't they? What I see right now is an airline that is trying to play catch-up by copying Delta and United.
transcript.zh: 天啊，他们以前还真出过一大堆不知所云的口号，对吧？我目前看到的是，一家试图通过模仿达美和美联航来拼命追赶的航司。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And these org changes are helpful. Seatback screens are helpful. Goldfish are helpful. But it doesn't solve everything.
transcript.zh: 这些组织架构调整是有益的，椅背屏是有益的，哪怕是小金鱼饼干也是有益的。但这解决不了一切。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There are still the intangibles that create excitement and loyalty: that involves an engaged front line, it involves just an overall image—the stuff you've been talking about. American isn't at that point. There's still more work to do, and I just wish there was more urgency behind it.
transcript.zh: 真正激发旅客热情和忠诚度的，依然是那些无形资产：这需要全情投入的一线员工，需要一个全面的品牌形象——也就是你一直在聊的那些。美航现在还没走到那一步。他们还有很多硬仗要打，我只是希望他们能展现出更强的紧迫感。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You've been listening to The Air Show. If you have suggestions or questions for us, or if you're interested in sponsoring the podcast, email us at info@theairshowpodcast.com, or visit theairshowpodcast.com.
transcript.zh: 感谢收听 The Air Show。如果您对我们有任何建议或疑问，或者有兴趣赞助本节目，请发邮件至 info@theairshowpodcast.com，或访问 our 网站 theairshowpodcast.com。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: cast.com to get in touch.
transcript.zh: cast.com 与我们取得联系。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Thanks to our sponsor Upgrade Inc. Learn more at upgrade.com/flex-pay.
transcript.zh: 感谢我们的赞助商 Upgrade Inc.。欲了解更多信息，请访问 upgrade.com/flex-pay。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Leo Duran produced and edited this episode. Our theme music is by Joshua Mosier. Thanks for listening, and we'll be back in a couple of weeks after our break.
transcript.zh: 本期节目由 Leo Duran 制作与剪辑。我们的主题曲由 Joshua Mosier 创作。感谢您的收听，休假结束后我们几周后再见。

transcript.speaker: Guest
transcript.en: We're American Airlines, something special in the air.
transcript.zh: 我们是美国航空，空中非凡体验。

vocab_notes.note_zh: 航空业专指对现有飞机客舱的座椅布局、内饰或机上娱乐设施进行重构升级的工程。
指自费购买头等舱、商务舱或超经的非因公度假旅客群体，是疫后航司收入增长的核心动力。
美国政治与文化常用语，指居住在东西两岸大都市、轻视或脱离中部地区（Middle America）偏好的人士。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 直飞州 / 中部被忽略的州
vocab_notes.note_zh: 美国口语中指从东海岸飞往西海岸时直接飞过的广袤中部州，常暗指非核心枢纽或非商旅核心的二三线市场。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 终极圣杯 / 最梦寐以求的终极目标
vocab_notes.note_zh: 常用于商业或技术领域，形容大家孜孜以求、一旦做成能带来巨大回报的终极方案（如机载广告精准投放变现）。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 职衔通胀 / 头衔膨胀
vocab_notes.note_zh: 职场术语，指企业内部滥发高大上的管理头衔（如向 CCO 汇报的 Chief Customer Officer），使 Chief 头衔贬值。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 伺候两位上司 / 双重汇报
vocab_notes.note_zh: 典故出自《圣经》，企业语境中指员工或部门同时向两个汇报线上司汇报时面临的权责冲突与协调困境。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 使某人措手不及 / 让人大吃一惊、陷入混乱
vocab_notes.note_zh: 美式口语常用俚语，形容突如其来的巨变或消息让人始料不及、阵脚大乱。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 故意拖延节奏 / 缓慢推进
vocab_notes.note_zh: 美式政商俚语，形容口头喊着紧急但实际操作中却分批次、慢条斯理地拖着推进改革或决策。

references.title: Kinective Media
references.creator: United Airlines
references.note_zh: 美联航设立的机载屏幕与数字化个性化广告媒体网络，节目中讨论美航前 CCO Vasu Raja 离职后曾参与运营此项目以实现机上屏幕流量变现。
